title: Which free ETL tool fits you?

questions.q: Who is going to run it?
questions.hint: Free software has no licence fee, but you pay in servers and people. A free plan has no servers to run.

options.label: A vendor should run it for us
options.why: you want a vendor-run free plan

options.label: We can run servers, even Kubernetes
We write Python code
options.why: dlt is a Python library you control in code

options.label: Pipelines as files in Git
options.why: Meltano is built around files in version control

questions.q: How much data will you move?
questions.hint: Free plans stop at a quota. Free software has no limit from the vendor.

options.label: Small: a few tables, low volume
options.why: small volumes fit inside a free plan

options.label: Large or growing fast
options.why: self-hosted tools have no limit from the vendor

options.label: SaaS apps and many different connectors
options.why: you need app connectors, and Debezium and OLake Go read databases

options.label: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server
options.why: these databases can be read by log

options.label: Oracle, with change capture
options.why: Debezium and Estuary read Oracle by log, and Fivetran's free plan excludes Oracle

options.label: Apache Iceberg tables in storage I own
Somewhere else, such as a warehouse
options.why: OLake Go writes Iceberg and Parquet, and our docs say warehouses can read its Iceberg tables

questions.q: How fresh does the data need to be?

options.label: As close to live as possible
options.why: you want a continuous stream of changes

airbyte.name: Airbyte Core
airbyte.summary: Free self-hosted software with over 600 pre-built connectors, per Airbyte's docs, and no limit on volume, users or connections.
airbyte.bestWhen: you need a large connector library and can run Kubernetes.
airbyte.watchOut: the Elastic License 2.0 is not a standard open-source licence, it is built to run on Kubernetes, and change capture runs as scheduled syncs, not a live stream.

meltano.name: Meltano
meltano.summary: MIT-licensed, command-line pipelines that live in version control.
meltano.bestWhen: your team likes the command line, Git and code review.
meltano.watchOut: connector quality varies, and we found no official Iceberg loader on its Hub.

dlt.name: dlt
dlt.summary: An Apache 2.0 Python library you add to a script, not a server you deploy.
dlt.bestWhen: your team writes Python and wants full control.
dlt.watchOut: something else has to run and schedule your script, and its docs do not describe binlog or redo-log change capture for MySQL or Oracle (checked Oct 2026).

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: Open-source change data capture that turns each database change into an event.
debezium.bestWhen: you already run Kafka and want one stream to feed many consumers.
debezium.watchOut: it only extracts, so you need something else to load the events, and its Iceberg sink is a community project.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Free, Apache 2.0 software that copies database changes into Apache Iceberg or Parquet on storage you own.
olake.bestWhen: you run PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server and want Iceberg tables you control.
olake.watchOut: change capture covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and SQL Server, Oracle, Db2 and S3 load by full refresh or incremental runs, and output is Iceberg and Parquet.

fivetran.name: Fivetran Free
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run free plan with 500,000 monthly active rows and all Standard-plan features.
fivetran.bestWhen: your volumes are low and you want a vendor to run everything.
fivetran.watchOut: Oracle, SAP and Db2 sources are not on the free plan, and Standard per-row rates sit in a separate table.

hevo.name: Hevo Free
hevo.summary: A free plan with 1M events a month, hourly runs and up to 5 users.
hevo.bestWhen: a small team wants a first managed pipeline for a few sources.
hevo.watchOut: Free covers only some connectors, and its pages describe no self-hosted edition.

estuary.name: Estuary Free
estuary.summary: A free plan with 10 GB a month and 2 connector instances, with no card needed.
estuary.bestWhen: you want to try a real-time pipeline with one source and one destination.
estuary.watchOut: one pipeline uses both free instances, the licence is Business Source License 1.1, and Iceberg needs extra AWS setup.
